why: The same root cause as RC3-01 with a different required contract, so a fix aimed only at `forall` leaves it open. The walker reached every value of every node except `op`, so a conjunct placed in a slot that is not a predicate position at all -- `present`'s `value`, which primitive-registry.json types JsonValue -- was still reported negated=False disjoined=False, which is to say DEMANDED. This fixture buries each of the three pinned conjuncts of criterion.SalesAgreement.performed.v1 inside `present(value: ...)`. Nothing is removed, nothing is disjoined, pin file and prose untouched. Measured before the repair with CONTRACTS_FIXTURE_RUN=1 at exit 0, 269,694 checks, every registry-level check passing. The validator must reject it saying the op sits in a NON-PREDICATE POSITION: as a requirement it is not present, and telling a reader it is missing would send them looking for an op that is right there in the body.
expect_failure_contains: PINNED CONJUNCT IN A NON-PREDICATE POSITION
note: `present(value: <a boolean op>)` is accepted by ast_check because the node's key set is exactly {op, value} and values.schema.json's JsonValue admits the object -- which is the point: the AST is not where this is caught, and typing alone does not catch it. What catches it is `argument_positions` in primitive-registry.json declaring `present.value` a `value` role, and the walk marking everything below a value slot as not-a-conjunct.
